name: Band Pull-Apart
description: The band pull-apart is a simple but highly effective prehabilitation exercise for the posterior shoulder and upper back. Holding a resistance band at arm's length, the exerciser pulls the band apart horizontally until it touches the chest, training the posterior deltoid, rhomboids, and middle trapezius. It is widely used as a warm-up drill, corrective exercise, and high-rep accessory movement for shoulder health.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a resistance band at both ends with both arms extended straight in front of the body at approximately shoulder height. Palms face the floor. Hands are slightly wider than shoulder-width.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose a resistance band light enough to maintain good form for high reps. Choke up on a heavier band to increase resistance, or use a lighter band for more range.
steps: Step 1: Hold the band with both hands at shoulder height, arms extended in front.
Step 2: Keeping the arms straight (slight elbow bend allowed), exhale and pull the band apart by moving both hands outward and back.
Step 3: Continue until the band touches the chest, squeezing the rear delts and rhomboids at peak contraction.
Step 4: Inhale and slowly return the hands to the starting extended position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull apart; inhale as you return.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows heavily during the pull, which reduces the targeted muscles' load
Internally rotating the shoulders — keep thumbs slightly elevated (external rotation)
safety_considerations: Select band resistance you can control — do not let the band snap back
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Pull until the band touches or nearly touches the sternum; return to fully extended arms.
coaching_cues: Lead with your elbows behind you as you pull the band apart
Think about bending the band around your chest — not just pulling the ends apart
